newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: CARACAS BUS FARES TO RISE 40 PCT ON AUG 15 - MAYOR.
newsitem.headline: CARACAS BUS FARES TO RISE 40 PCT ON AUG 15 - MAYOR.

text.p: The main municipality in the Venezuelan capital reached an agreement with public transport companies under which bus fares will rise by 40 percent from Aug 15, Caracas Mayor Antonio Ledezma told reporters.
Bus fares are an highly sensitive issue in Venezuela and hikes have in the past led to violent protests, particularly by students.
In return for the increase in minimum fares from 50 to 70 bolivars ($0.14), bus companies have pledged to repair and upgrade their vehicles, Ledezma said.
From October buses classified as in "optimum condition" will be allowed to charge a minimum fare of 80 bolivars ($0.16). The price would rise to 100 bolivars ($0.20) in December, he said.

Bus fares in Venezuela are heavily subsidized. Although gasoline prices are just 70 bolivars ($0.14) per liter, drivers receive a monthly subsidy of 108,000 bolivars ($220) for fuel and another $20,000 ($40) to compensate for cheaper student fares.
